name: Jawline Consistency
description: Analyzes jaw boundary smoothness and consistency
mechanism:
This method analyzes jawline characteristics for video deepfake detection:

1. **Jawline Contour Tracking**: The mandibular contour is tracked per frame using facial landmarks from chin point through jaw angles to ear attachment points. The contour is parameterized by curvature, angular measurements at the gonial angle, and chin shape.

2. **Jaw-Neck Transition Analysis**: The boundary where the jaw meets the neck is a critical deepfake artifact zone. Natural jaw-neck transitions show anatomically correct tissue layering (skin, platysma muscle, subcutaneous fat). The method analyzes this transition for blending artifacts, color discontinuities, or unnatural sharp/smooth boundaries.

3. **Jaw Motion Biomechanics**: During speech, the mandible rotates on the temporomandibular joint with specific biomechanical constraints (hinge + sliding motion, maximum opening ~40mm). The method verifies that jaw motion during speech follows these constraints. Deepfakes may produce jaw motion that violates TMJ biomechanics.

4. **Jawline Symmetry Consistency**: Mandibular asymmetry is a stable individual characteristic. The method tracks left-right jawline correspondence across frames — the asymmetry pattern should remain constant. Deepfakes may produce varying jaw asymmetry as the generator independently renders each frame.

5. **Jawline Resolution Assessment**: The jawline is often at the boundary of the face-swap region. The method compares rendering quality of the jawline itself versus adjacent regions — resolution drops, texture quality changes, or sharpness discontinuities at the jawline indicate the edge of a generated face region.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through jawline consistency analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Rossler, A. et al. (2019). FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images. ICCV.
Li, Y. et al. (2020). Face X-ray for More General Face Forgery Detection. CVPR.
